## Data Preperation and Segmentation

```{r}
d1 <- read.table("./data/student-mat.csv", 
                 sep = ";", 
                 header = TRUE)
d2 <- read.table("./data/student-por.csv", 
                 sep = ";", 
                 header = TRUE)
d3=merge(d1,d2,by=c("school","sex","age","address","famsize","Pstatus","Medu","Fedu","Mjob",
                    "Fjob","reason","nursery","internet"))
nrow(d3) # 382 students
unique(d3$school) #gp and ms
unique(d3$age) #15 16 17 18 19 20 22
summary(d3)

library(dplyr)
#### Resolve Data Leakage & Redundancy
# Remove the Portuguese-specific columns (.y) and clean the Math column names (.x).
# This ensures the model isn't confused by having the same data twice, especially with the
# tree considering that it is very sensitive to the datapoints.
df_clean <- d3 %>% 
   select(-ends_with(".y")) %>%
   rename_with(~gsub(".x", "", .x), ends_with(".x"))
summary(df_clean)

# Instead of predicting the final grade, we predict the 'Progress' delta.
# This forces the model to explain why a student improved or declined as opposed to just
# saying if you failed in the past you will fail again
# G3_diff > 0 means the student improved since the midterm
df_clean$G3_progress <- df_clean$G3 - df_clean$G2

# The summary showed max absences of 75. cap it to prevent a skewed tree - A student with
# 75 absences is an extreme outlier. In a Decision Tree, extreme outliers create 'pure'
# but useless branches that don't generalize. Capping at 30 stabilizes the variance of
# the 'absences' variable.
df_clean$absences <- ifelse(df_clean$absences > 30, 30, df_clean$absences)

# Binary Transform (Making Yes/No 1/0 for cleaner splits) - Helps set up for the decision
# tree and makes it less viable for the decision tree to get confused
char_to_binary <- c("schoolsup", "famsup", "paid", "activities", "nursery", "higher",
                    "internet", "romantic")
df_clean[char_to_binary] <- lapply(df_clean[char_to_binary], 
                                   function(x) ifelse(x == "yes", 1, 0))
df_clean <- df_clean %>% mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
df_preemptive <- df_clean %>% select(-G1, -G2)

hist(df_preemptive$G3)
table(df_preemptive$G3)

df_preemptive <- df_clean %>% select(-G1, -G2) %>% filter(G3 > 0)

#### Creating the Sub segments
# d1 is the math data
# d2 is the portuguese data

d1_math_clean <- d1
d1_math_clean$absences <- ifelse(d1_math_clean$absences > 30, 30, d1_math_clean$absences)
d1_math_clean$G3_progress <- d1_math_clean$G3-d1_math_clean$G2
char_to_binary <- c("schoolsup", "famsup", "paid", "activities", "nursery", "higher",
                    "internet", "romantic")
d1_math_clean[char_to_binary] <- lapply(d1_math_clean[char_to_binary],
                                        function(x) ifelse(x == "yes", 1, 0))

d2_port_clean <- d2
d2_port_clean$absences <- ifelse(d2_port_clean$absences > 30, 30, d2_port_clean$absences)
d2_port_clean$G3_progress <- d2_port_clean$G3-d2_port_clean$G2
char_to_binary <- c("schoolsup", "famsup", "paid", "activities", "nursery", "higher",
                    "internet", "romantic")
d2_port_clean[char_to_binary] <- lapply(d2_port_clean[char_to_binary],
                                        function(x) ifelse(x == "yes", 1, 0))

summary(d1_math_clean$G3_progress)
# Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max. 
# -10.0000   0.0000   0.0000  -0.2987   1.0000   3.0000

summary(d2_port_clean$G3_progress)
# Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max. 
# -9.0000  0.0000  0.0000  0.3359  1.0000  6.0000

#### Segmentation Strategy
# Declining: Less than 0 (e.g., -10 to -1)
# Stable: Exactly 0
# Improving: Greater than 0 (e.g., 1 to 6)

# For Math Data
d1_math_clean <- d1_math_clean %>%
  mutate(progress_segment = cut(G3_progress, 
                                breaks = c(-Inf, -0.1, 0.1, Inf), 
                                labels = c("Declining", "Stable", "Improving")))
# For Portuguese Data
d2_port_clean <- d2_port_clean %>%
  mutate(progress_segment = cut(G3_progress, 
                                breaks = c(-Inf, -0.1, 0.1, Inf), 
                                labels = c("Declining", "Stable", "Improving")))

df_preemptive_math <- d1_math_clean %>% select(-G1, -G2) %>% filter(G3 > 0)
df_preemptive_port <- d2_port_clean %>% select(-G1, -G2) %>% filter(G3 > 0)
```

## Decision Tree

```{r, error=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
set.seed(123)

# MATH: Final Grade Prediction 
tree_math_social <- tree(G3 ~ ., data = df_preemptive_math)
plot(tree_math_social)
text(tree_math_social, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)
title("Math: Social Factors & Final Grade")

# Pruning Math Tree
cv_math <- cv.tree(tree_math_social)
cv_math
tree_math_pruned <- prune.tree(tree_math_social, best = 7) 
plot(tree_math_pruned)
text(tree_math_pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)

# MATH: Progress Prediction
# Removing G3 to avoid leakage when predicting progress
math_progress_data <- df_preemptive_math %>% select(-G3, -progress_segment)
tree_math_move <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = math_progress_data)
plot(tree_math_move)
text(tree_math_move, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)
title("Math: Factors Predicting Improvement/Decline")

# Pruning Math Social Tree
cv_math_social <- cv.tree(tree_math_move)
cv_math_social
tree_math_pruned_social <- prune.tree(tree_math_social, best = 2) 
plot(tree_math_pruned_social)
text(tree_math_pruned_social, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)


set.seed(123)

# PORTUGUESE: Final Grade Prediction
tree_port_social <- tree(G3 ~ ., data = df_preemptive_port)
plot(tree_port_social)
text(tree_port_social, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)
title("Portuguese: Social Factors & Final Grade")
cv_port <- cv.tree(tree_port_social)
cv_port
tree_port_pruned <- prune.tree(tree_port_social, best = 4) 
plot(tree_port_pruned)
text(tree_port_pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)

# PORTUGUESE: Progress Prediction 
port_progress_data <- df_preemptive_port %>% select(-G3, -progress_segment)
# tree_port_move <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = port_progress_data) 
# - in plot.tree(tree_port_move) : cannot plot singlenode tree

# Math is "Sensitive" to Social Factors: In the Math dataset (d1), variables like failures
# and schoolsup successfully predicted grade movement. 
# This suggests that a student's environment and past academic record have a high impact
# on their Math progress.

# Portuguese is "Resilient" to Social Factors: The "singlenode" error proves that for the
# Portuguese class (d2), factors like family relationships, parents' jobs, and even
# past failures could not reliably predict whether a student improved or declined.

# The Interpretation: We could argue that Portuguese (a native language subject) is less
# dependent on the specific social/behavioral "shocks" measured in this dataset compared
# to a cumulative technical subject like Math.

#### Math: Additional Breakdown
math_declining <- df_preemptive_math %>% 
  filter(progress_segment == "Declining") %>%
  select(-G3, -progress_segment)
math_stable <- df_preemptive_math %>% 
  filter(progress_segment == "Stable") %>%
  select(-G3, -progress_segment)
math_improving <- df_preemptive_math %>%
  filter(progress_segment == "Improving") %>%
  select(-G3, -progress_segment)

tree_math_declining <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = math_declining)
tree_math_stable    <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = math_stable)
tree_math_improving <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = math_improving)

cv_math_declining <- cv.tree(tree_math_declining)
cv_math_stable    <- cv.tree(tree_math_stable)
cv_math_improving <- cv.tree(tree_math_improving)

tree_math_declining_pruned <- prune.tree(tree_math_declining,
      best = cv_math_declining$size[which.min(cv_math_declining$dev)])
tree_math_stable_pruned <- prune.tree(tree_math_stable,
      best = max(2, cv_math_stable$size[which.min(cv_math_stable$dev)]))
tree_math_improving_pruned <- prune.tree(tree_math_improving, 
      best = max(2, cv_math_improving$size[which.min(cv_math_improving$dev)]))

# Then plot all three
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(tree_math_declining_pruned);
text(tree_math_declining_pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7);
title("Math | Declining")
plot(tree_math_stable_pruned);
text(tree_math_stable_pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7);
title("Math | Stable")
plot(tree_math_improving_pruned); 
text(tree_math_improving_pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7);
title("Math | Improving")

#### Port: Additional Breakdown
port_declining <- df_preemptive_port %>%
  filter(progress_segment == "Declining") %>%
  select(-G3, -progress_segment)
port_stable <- df_preemptive_port %>%
  filter(progress_segment == "Stable") %>%
  select(-G3, -progress_segment)
port_improving <- df_preemptive_port %>%
  filter(progress_segment == "Improving") %>%
  select(-G3, -progress_segment)

tree_port_declining <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = port_declining)
tree_port_stable    <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = port_stable)
tree_port_improving <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = port_improving)

cv_port_declining <- cv.tree(tree_port_declining)
cv_port_stable    <- cv.tree(tree_port_stable)
cv_port_improving <- cv.tree(tree_port_improving)

tree_port_declining_pruned <- prune.tree(tree_port_declining,
      best = cv_port_declining$size[which.min(cv_port_declining$dev)])
tree_port_declining_pruned <- prune.tree(tree_port_declining, 
      best = max(2, cv_port_declining$size[which.min(cv_port_declining$dev)]))
tree_port_improving_pruned <- prune.tree(tree_port_improving,
      best = max(2, cv_port_improving$size[which.min(cv_port_improving$dev)]))

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(tree_port_declining_pruned);
text(tree_port_declining_pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7);
title("Portuguese | Declining")
plot(tree_port_stable_pruned);
text(tree_port_stable_pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7);
title("Portuguese | Stable")
plot(tree_port_improving_pruned);
text(tree_port_improving_pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7);
title("Portuguese | Improving")

# MATH tree_social RMSE
math_pred <- predict(tree_math_pruned, df_preemptive_math)
math_rmse <- sqrt(mean((df_preemptive_math$G3 - math_pred)^2))
cat("Math tree_social RMSE:", math_rmse)

# MATH tree_move RMSE
math_move_pred <- predict(tree_math_pruned_social, math_progress_data)

cat("Math tree_move RMSE:", math_move_rmse)

# PORTUGUESE tree_social RMSE
```

## PCA + Decision Tree

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# SECTION 3.1: PREPARE NUMERIC-ONLY FEATURES FOR PCA
# We drop the targets (G3, G3_progress, progress_segment) so the PCA captures student
# background factors only, not outcomes, preventing leakage into the components.

# Pull only numeric predictor columns for Math
math_features <- df_preemptive_math %>%
  select(-G3, -G3_progress, -progress_segment) %>%
  select(where(is.numeric))

# Pull only numeric predictor columns for Portuguese
port_features <- df_preemptive_port %>%
  select(-G3, -G3_progress, -progress_segment) %>%
  select(where(is.numeric))

# Check means and variances before scaling 
apply(math_features, 2, mean)
apply(math_features, 2, var)

apply(port_features, 2, mean)
apply(port_features, 2, var)

# Scale both datasets (mean = 0, sd = 1)
# Required before PCA so variables on different scales don't dominate
Math.Scaled <- scale(math_features)
Port.Scaled <- scale(port_features)

# SECTION 3.2: RUN PCA
# scale = TRUE standardizes variables

# Run PCA on Math features
pr.math <- prcomp(math_features, scale = TRUE)

# Run PCA on Portuguese features
pr.port <- prcomp(port_features, scale = TRUE)

# Inspect the PCA objects
names(pr.math)
names(pr.port)

# We ran the following lines in the original code of course but we have commented it
# out here to save you from having to scroll through 20+ pages of loading vectors
# and PC scores.

pr.math$center    # raw variable means (Math)
pr.math$scale     # raw variable SDs   (Math)
# pr.math$rotation  # loading vectors    (Math) — which features drive each PC
# pr.math$x         # PC scores          (Math) — each student's position on each PC

pr.port$center
pr.port$scale
# pr.port$rotation  # loading vectors (Portuguese)
# pr.port$x         # PC scores       (Portuguese)

# Full summary: SDs, % variance, cumulative % variance
summary(pr.math)
summary(pr.port)

# SECTION 3.3: VARIANCE EXPLAINED + SCREE PLOTS

# Compute PC variances (eigenvalues)
pr.var.math <- pr.math$sdev^2
pr.var.port <- pr.port$sdev^2

# Total variance should equal number of features (all scaled to var = 1)
sum(pr.var.math)
sum(pr.var.port)

# Proportion of Variance Explained (PVE)
pve.math <- pr.var.math / sum(pr.var.math)
pve.port <- pr.var.port / sum(pr.var.port)

pve.math
pve.port

# Scree plots: PVE and Cumulative PVE
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

plot(pve.math,
     xlab = "Principal Component",
     ylab = "Proportion of Variance Explained",
     ylim = c(0, 1), type = "b",
     main = "Math: PVE by Component")

plot(cumsum(pve.math),
     xlab = "Principal Component",
     ylab = "Cumulative Proportion of Variance Explained",
     ylim = c(0, 1), type = "b",
     main = "Math: Cumulative PVE")

plot(pve.port,
     xlab = "Principal Component",
     ylab = "Proportion of Variance Explained",
     ylim = c(0, 1), type = "b",
     main = "Portuguese: PVE by Component")

plot(cumsum(pve.port),
     xlab = "Principal Component",
     ylab = "Cumulative Proportion of Variance Explained",
     ylim = c(0, 1), type = "b",
     main = "Portuguese: Cumulative PVE")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# SECTION 3.4: BIPLOTS
# Visualize which features load most heavily on PC1 and PC2

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
biplot(pr.math, center = TRUE, scale = 0, cex = 0.5,
       main = "Math: PCA Biplot (PC1 vs PC2)")
biplot(pr.port, center = TRUE, scale = 0, cex = 0.5,
       main = "Portuguese: PCA Biplot (PC1 vs PC2)")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Print loadings to see which variables drive each PC
pr.math$rotation  # Math loadings
pr.port$rotation  # Portuguese loadings

# SECTION 3.5: COMBINE PC SCORES WITH SCALED DATA

# Combine scaled features + all PC scores into one dataframe
Math.PCscores <- data.frame(Math.Scaled, pr.math$x)
Port.PCscores <- data.frame(Port.Scaled, pr.port$x)

View(Math.PCscores)
View(Port.PCscores)

# Verify: manually compute PC1 score for student 1 (Math)
# PC1 score = sum of (loading * scaled feature value) across all features
# This should match pr.math$x[1, 1]
Student1.Math.PC1 <- sum(pr.math$rotation[, 1] * Math.Scaled[1, ])
Student1.Math.PC1 # 0.4249391
pr.math$x[1, 1]  # should match & it does match

# SECTION 3.6: CHOOSE NUMBER OF PCs TO KEEP
# Rule: keep enough PCs to explain at least 80% of variance.

# How many PCs does it take to hit 80% for Math?
which(cumsum(pve.math) >= 0.80)[1] #14

# How many PCs does it take to hit 80% for Portuguese?
which(cumsum(pve.port) >= 0.80)[1] #14

# Store the cutoffs
npc_math <- which(cumsum(pve.math) >= 0.80)[1]
npc_port <- which(cumsum(pve.port) >= 0.80)[1]

cat("Math: PCs needed for 80% variance =", npc_math, "\n") 
# Math: PCs needed for 80% variance = 14 

cat("Portuguese: PCs needed for 80% variance =", npc_port, "\n") 
# Portuguese: PCs needed for 80% variance = 14 

# Note the answers are the same for both 

# SECTION 3.7: BUILD TREE-READY DATASETS FROM PC SCORES

# Math: select top PCs + attach target
math_tree_df <- data.frame(pr.math$x[, 1:npc_math])
math_tree_df$G3_progress <- df_preemptive_math$G3_progress

# Portuguese: select top PCs + attach target
port_tree_df <- data.frame(pr.port$x[, 1:npc_port])
port_tree_df$G3_progress <- df_preemptive_port$G3_progress

View(math_tree_df)
View(port_tree_df)

# SECTION 3.8: DECISION TREE ON PCA COMPONENTS
# Predict G3_progress from PC scores.

set.seed(123)

# MATH: Full Tree on PCA Components 

tree.math.pca <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = math_tree_df)
plot(tree.math.pca)
text(tree.math.pca, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)
title("Math: G3 Progress Predicted from PCA Components")

summary(tree.math.pca)

# MATH: Cross-Validate and Prune
cv.math.pca <- cv.tree(tree.math.pca)
cv.math.pca

# Find the optimal tree size (fewest nodes at lowest deviance)
best.math.pca <- cv.math.pca$size[which.min(cv.math.pca$dev)]
best.math.pca <- max(2, best.math.pca)  # ensure at least 2 terminal nodes
cat("Math PCA tree: optimal size =", best.math.pca, "\n")

tree.math.pca.pruned <- prune.tree(tree.math.pca, best = best.math.pca)
plot(tree.math.pca.pruned)
text(tree.math.pca.pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)
title("Math: Pruned PCA Tree — G3 Progress")


# MATH: RMSE

math.pca.pred <- predict(tree.math.pca.pruned, math_tree_df)
math.pca.rmse <- sqrt(mean((math_tree_df$G3_progress - math.pca.pred)^2))
cat("Math PCA Tree RMSE:", math.pca.rmse, "\n")
# Math PCA Tree RMSE: 0.8028644 

# PORTUGUESE: Full Tree on PCA Components 

set.seed(123)
tree.port.pca <- tree(G3_progress ~ ., data = port_tree_df)
plot(tree.port.pca)
text(tree.port.pca, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)
title("Portuguese: G3 Progress Predicted from PCA Components")

summary(tree.port.pca)


# PORTUGUESE: Cross-Validate and Prune

cv.port.pca <- cv.tree(tree.port.pca)
cv.port.pca

best.port.pca <- cv.port.pca$size[which.min(cv.port.pca$dev)]
best.port.pca <- max(2, best.port.pca)
cat("Portuguese PCA tree: optimal size =", best.port.pca, "\n")

tree.port.pca.pruned <- prune.tree(tree.port.pca, best = best.port.pca)
plot(tree.port.pca.pruned)
text(tree.port.pca.pruned, pretty = 0, cex = 0.7)
title("Portuguese: Pruned PCA Tree — G3 Progress")


# PORTUGUESE: RMSE 

port.pca.pred <- predict(tree.port.pca.pruned, port_tree_df)
port.pca.rmse <- sqrt(mean((port_tree_df$G3_progress - port.pca.pred)^2))
cat("Portuguese PCA Tree RMSE:", port.pca.rmse, "\n")
#Portuguese PCA Tree RMSE: 0.9530515


# math.raw.rmse <- 2.781059
# port.raw.rmse <- 2.300445

table(tree.math.pca.pruned$frame$var)
table(tree.port.pca.pruned$frame$var)
```

#### Random Forest


```{r rf}
d1_math_clean <- d1

# Cap absences at 30 (same cutoff as DT)
d1_math_clean$absences <- ifelse(d1_math_clean$absences > 30, 30, d1_math_clean$absences)

# Engineer G3_progress = G3 - G2
d1_math_clean$G3_progress <- d1_math_clean$G3 - d1_math_clean$G2

# Binary encode yes/no columns
char_to_binary <- c("schoolsup", "famsup", "paid", "activities",
                    "nursery", "higher", "internet", "romantic")
d1_math_clean[char_to_binary] <- lapply(
  d1_math_clean[char_to_binary],
  function(x) ifelse(x == "yes", 1, 0)
)

# Convert remaining character columns to factors 
d1_math_clean <- d1_math_clean %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

# Remove G1, G2 and filter G3=0 dropouts
df_preemptive_math <- d1_math_clean %>%
  select(-G1, -G2) %>%
  filter(G3 > 0)

cat("Math after cleaning:", nrow(df_preemptive_math), "\n") # 357

# STEP 3: Clean Portuguese data 
d2_port_clean <- d2

d2_port_clean$absences <- ifelse(d2_port_clean$absences > 30, 30, d2_port_clean$absences)
d2_port_clean$G3_progress <- d2_port_clean$G3 - d2_port_clean$G2

d2_port_clean[char_to_binary] <- lapply(
  d2_port_clean[char_to_binary],
  function(x) ifelse(x == "yes", 1, 0)
)

d2_port_clean <- d2_port_clean %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

df_preemptive_port <- d2_port_clean %>%
  select(-G1, -G2) %>%
  filter(G3 > 0)

cat("Portuguese after cleaning:", nrow(df_preemptive_port), "\n")#634

## ── STEP 3: Create progress_segment ─────────────────────────
# Reuse DT teammate's segmentation logic exactly:
#   Declining:  G3_progress < 0
#   Stable:     G3_progress = 0
#   Improving:  G3_progress > 0

# Math
df_preemptive_math$progress_segment <- cut(
  df_preemptive_math$G3_progress,
  breaks = c(-Inf, -0.1, 0.1, Inf),
  labels = c("Declining", "Stable", "Improving")
)

# Portuguese
df_preemptive_port$progress_segment <- cut(
  df_preemptive_port$G3_progress,
  breaks = c(-Inf, -0.1, 0.1, Inf),
  labels = c("Declining", "Stable", "Improving")
)

# Check distribution — see how many students fall in each category
cat("===== Math progress_segment distribution =====\n")
print(table(df_preemptive_math$progress_segment))
print(prop.table(table(df_preemptive_math$progress_segment)))
# Declining    Stable Improving 
# 65       181       111 

# Declining    Stable Improving 
# 0.1820728 0.5070028 0.3109244 

# Among 357 Math students, 65 regressed (18.2%), 181 remained the same (50.7%), and 111
# improved (31.1%).

cat("\n===== Portuguese progress_segment distribution =====\n")
print(table(df_preemptive_port$progress_segment))
print(prop.table(table(df_preemptive_port$progress_segment)))
# Declining    Stable Improving 
# 64       280       290 

# Declining    Stable Improving 
# 0.1009464 0.4416404 0.4574132 

# There were 634 students studying Portuguese: 64 saw their marks drop (10.1%), 280
# remained the same (44.2%), and 290 improved (45.7%). This suggests that performance
# in Portuguese, as a subject taught in the students’ mother tongue, is more stable,
# and students are less likely to see their marks drop. The proportion of students who
# improved was higher (45.7% compared to 31.1% in Maths), with nearly half of the
# students showing improvement.

# STEP 4: BUILD 4 RF MODELS randomForest
# When you write `importance = TRUE`, after building 500 trees, the RF performs an
# additional round of calculations: it shuffles each variable individually, measures
# the increase in error, and stores the results in the model object. When you
# subsequently call `varImpPlot(rf_social_math, type = 1)`, it retrieves the data from
# these stored results to plot the graph.
# ============================================================
# Structure mirrors DT exactly:
#   rf_social → predict G3 (where will student end up?)
#   rf_move   → predict G3_progress (how much will they move?)
#
# IMPORTANT: must remove G3_progress when predicting G3 (and vice versa)
#            otherwise one target leaks into the other

# ── 4A: rf_social_math ──────────────────────────────────────
# Target: G3 (final grade)
# Remove: G3_progress (derived from G3, would leak)

set.seed(123)
rf_social_math <- randomForest(
     G3 ~ .,
     data       = df_preemptive_math %>% select(-G3_progress),
     ntree      = 500,
     importance = TRUE)     # needed for %IncMSE plot)
print(rf_social_math)
#  Mean of squared residuals → 8.421954
#          % Var explained → 18.94

# ── 4B: rf_social_port ──────────────────────────────────────
# Target: G3 (final grade)
# Same setup, different dataset

set.seed(123)
rf_social_port <- randomForest(
     G3 ~ .,
     data       = df_preemptive_port %>% select(-G3_progress),
     ntree      = 500,
     importance = TRUE)
print(rf_social_port)
#  Mean of squared residuals → 4.652499
#          % Var explained → 35.69

# ── 4C: rf_move_math Build classification RF models────────────────────────────────────────
# Remove G3 (data leakage) and G3_progress (target is derived from it)
# Keep progress_segment as the target
# randomForest auto-detects classification when target is a factor

# rf_move_math (classification)
set.seed(42)
rf_move_math <- randomForest(
     progress_segment ~ .,
     data       = df_preemptive_math %>% select(-G3, -G3_progress),
     ntree      = 500,
     importance = TRUE)

cat("\n===== rf_move_math (Classification) =====\n")
print(rf_move_math)
# Key outputs to note:
#   OOB estimate of error rate → 53.22%
#   Confusion matrix → shows where model gets it right/wrong
# Confusion matrix:
# Declining Stable Improving class.error
# Declining         3     56         6   0.9538462
# Stable            0    149        32   0.1767956
# Improving         0     96        15   0.8648649

# rf_move_port (classification)
set.seed(42)
rf_move_port <- randomForest(
     progress_segment ~ .,
     data       = df_preemptive_port %>% select(-G3, -G3_progress),
     ntree      = 500,
     importance = TRUE)

cat("\n===== rf_move_port (Classification) =====\n")
print(rf_move_port)
# Key outputs to note:
#   OOB estimate of error rate → 52.68%
# Confusion matrix:
# Declining Stable Improving class.error
# Declining         0     23        41   1.0000000
# Stable            1    134       145   0.5214286
# Improving         1    123       166   0.4275862


# STEP 5: 10-FOLD CROSS-VALIDATION RMSE
# ============================================================
# This gives honest out-of-sample RMSE
# Comparable to paper's method and to DT's cv.tree() results

cv_control <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10)

# rf_social_math CV
set.seed(123)
cv_social_math <- train(
     G3 ~ .,
     data      = df_preemptive_math %>% select(-G3_progress),
     method    = "rf",
     trControl = cv_control,
     ntree     = 500)
print(cv_social_math)

# rf_social_port CV
set.seed(123)
cv_social_port <- train(
     G3 ~ .,
     data      = df_preemptive_port %>% select(-G3_progress),
     method    = "rf",
     trControl = cv_control,
     ntree     = 500)

# ── 10-Fold CV Accuracy ─────────────────────────────
# Classification uses Accuracy instead of RMSE

cv_control <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10)

# rf_move_math CV
set.seed(42)
cv_move_math <- train(
     progress_segment ~ .,
     data      = df_preemptive_math %>% select(-G3, -G3_progress),
     method    = "rf",

     ntree     = 500)

cat("\n===== rf_move_math CV Results =====\n")
print(cv_move_math)
# Look at: Accuracy and Kappa   
# Kappa adjusts for class imbalance — more honest than raw accuracy
# mtry    Accuracy   Kappa       
#   2    0.4905491  -0.009955717

# rf_move_port CV
set.seed(42)
cv_move_port <- train(

#2    0.4982887  0.08922893

cat("rf_social_port CV RMSE:", round(min(cv_social_port$results$RMSE), 3), "\n")
#rf_social_port CV RMSE: 2.155


# STEP 6: VARIABLE IMPORTANCE PLOTS
# =========================================================

# In a randomised impact plot, for each variable (such as ‘failures’), RF shuffles the
# values of that variable across all samples and then re-runs the model to see by how
# much the prediction error increases. If the error skyrockets by 16% after shuffling
# ‘failures’, this indicates that the model is highly dependent on it, and it is
# therefore important. If the error remains virtually unchanged after shuffling a
# particular variable, this suggests that the model does not require it at all.

## type=1 → %IncMSE (how much error increases when variable is shuffled)
plot_importance_labeled <- function(rf_model, title, n.var = 15) {
     # abstract importance data
     imp <- importance(rf_model, type = 1)  # type=1 = %IncMSE
     imp_df <- data.frame(
          Variable = rownames(imp),
          IncMSE   = round(imp[, 1], 1))
     # Sort by importance and take the top n.var items
     imp_df <- imp_df[order(imp_df$IncMSE, decreasing = FALSE), ]
     imp_df <- tail(imp_df, n.var)  # Take the last n.var rows (the most important ones)
     # horizontal bar chart
     bp <- barplot(
          imp_df$IncMSE,
          names.arg = imp_df$Variable,
          horiz     = TRUE,           # horizontal 
          las       = 1,              # name
          col       = "#B5D4F4",      
          border    = "#185FA5",      
          xlab      = "%IncMSE",
          main      = title )
     #label
     text(
          x      = imp_df$IncMSE + max(imp_df$IncMSE) * 0.03,  
          y      = bp,
          labels = paste0(imp_df$IncMSE, "%"),
          cex    = 0.8,
          adj    = 0    )} # # Left-aligned 
varImpPlot(rf_social_math, type = 1, n.var = 5,
           main = "rf_social_math: Variable Importance\n(Predicting G3 — Math)")
varImpPlot(rf_social_port, type = 1, n.var = 5,
           main = "rf_social_port: Variable Importance
           \n(Predicting G3 — Portuguese)")
varImpPlot(rf_move_math, type = 1, n.var = 5,
           main = "rf_move_math: Variable Importance
           \n(Predicting Progress Direction — Math)")
varImpPlot(rf_move_port, type = 1, n.var = 5,
           main = "rf_move_port: Variable Importance
           \n(Predicting Progress Direction — Portuguese)")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# ggplot rf_social_math
imp <- importance(rf_social_math, type = 1)
imp_df <- data.frame(
     variable = rownames(imp),
     IncMSE   = imp[, 1]
)
imp_df <- imp_df %>% arrange(desc(IncMSE)) %>% head(5)

ggplot(imp_df, aes(x = reorder(variable, IncMSE), y = IncMSE)) +
     geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
     geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(IncMSE, 1), "%")),
               hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5) +
     coord_flip() +
     labs(title = "rf_social_math: Variable Importance",
          x = NULL, y = "%IncMSE") +
     theme_minimal()
# failures 16.8%，schoolsup 16.3%

# ggplot rf_social_port
imp2 <- importance(rf_social_port, type = 1)
imp2_df <- data.frame(
     variable = rownames(imp2),
     IncMSE   = imp2[, 1]
)
imp2_df <- imp2_df %>% arrange(desc(IncMSE)) %>% head(5)

ggplot(imp2_df, aes(x = reorder(variable, IncMSE), y = IncMSE)) +
     geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
     geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(IncMSE, 1), "%")),
               hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5) +
     coord_flip() +
     labs(title = "rf_social_port: Variable Importance",
          x = NULL, y = "%IncMSE") +
     theme_minimal()
# failures 38.1%， higher 25.4%

# ggplot rf_move_math
# Math
imp_math <- importance(rf_move_math, type = 1)
imp_math_df <- data.frame(
     variable = rownames(imp_math),
     MeanDecreaseAccuracy = imp_math[, "MeanDecreaseAccuracy"]
)
imp_math_df <- imp_math_df %>% arrange(desc(MeanDecreaseAccuracy)) %>% head(10)

ggplot(imp_math_df, aes(x = reorder(variable, MeanDecreaseAccuracy),
                        y = MeanDecreaseAccuracy)) +
     geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
     geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(MeanDecreaseAccuracy, 1), "%")),

     coord_flip() +
     labs(title = "rf_move_math: What Predicts Progress Direction?",
          subtitle = "Math — Declining vs Stable vs Improving",
          x = NULL, y = "Mean Decrease Accuracy") +
     theme_minimal()
# famrel = 4.9% health = 2.3%
```

```{r svm}
#### Running a SVM using all the data in order to see how accurate
#### the model is before the sub segments are utilized.
library(e1071)
library(kernlab)
library(caret)

set.seed(123)
a_df_preemptive <- df_preemptive %>%
   mutate(progress_segment = cut(G3_progress, 
                                 breaks = c(-Inf, -0.1, 0.1, Inf), 
                                 labels = c("Declining", "Stable", "Improving")))
a_splitting <- sample(1:nrow(a_df_preemptive), 0.8 * nrow(a_df_preemptive))
a_train_data <- a_df_preemptive[a_splitting, ]
a_test_data  <- a_df_preemptive[-a_splitting, ]

a_tuned <- tune(svm, progress_segment ~ . -G3 -G3_progress,
                data = a_train_data, kernel = "radial",
                ranges = list(cost  = c(0.1, 1, 10, 50, 100, 200),
                              gamma = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2)))

a_best_radial <- a_tuned$best.model

a_ypred_radial <- predict(a_best_radial, a_test_data)
a_test_table_radial <- table(Predicted = a_ypred_radial,
                             Actual = a_test_data$progress_segment)
#                       Actual
# Predicted   Declining Stable Improving
# Declining         0      0         0
# Stable           17     37        15
# Improving         0      0         0
a_correct_pred_radial <- sum(diag(a_test_table_radial)) / sum(a_test_table_radial)
a_error_rate_radial <- 1 - a_correct_pred_radial
cat("The error rate: ", a_error_rate_radial)
# The error rate:  0.4637681

### Running a SVM using the sub segments. There are two main packages for SVM
### work in R: e1071 and kernlab. They both produce SVMs but they use different
### code to do so. I am trying them both to see the results, first.

### For df_preemptive_math
set.seed(123)
m_splitting <- sample(1:nrow(df_preemptive_math), 0.8 * nrow(df_preemptive_math))
m_train_data <- df_preemptive_math[m_splitting, ]
m_test_data  <- df_preemptive_math[-m_splitting, ]

# using e1071
# Please note that the rminer package merely places a wrapper around the e1071
# package for SVM. This package is the one that did all the work under the hood
# for the paper.
em_tuned <- tune(svm, progress_segment ~ . -G3 -G3_progress,
                 data = m_train_data, kernel = "radial",
                 ranges = list(cost  = c(0.1, 1, 10, 50, 100, 200),

summary(em_tuned)

em_ypred_radial <- predict(em_best_radial, m_test_data)

em_error_rate_radial <- 1 - em_correct_pred_radial

# using kernlab
library(kernlab)
km_svm_model <- ksvm(progress_segment ~ . -G3 -G3_progress,

# These models are also just guessing since there's nothing there for the
# Declining section. But they are at least trying on Stable and Improving,
# which is a minor improvement from the Math section.

# There are two main issues that need to be rectified for the SVM to be useful
# for this data. The first is the class imbalance issue. The second is that
# the model needs to focus on the Declining portion, since it is needed
# for early intervention.

table(df_preemptive_math$progress_segment)
# Declining    Stable Improving 
#        65       181       111 
table(df_preemptive_port$progress_segment)
# Declining    Stable Improving 
#        64       280       290

library(caret)
library(kernlab)
shared_tune_grid <- expand.grid(
  sigma = c(0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15),
  C     = c(0.5, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100)
)
shared_preprocess <- c("center", "scale", "nzv")
shared_class_weights <- c("Declining" = 4, "Stable" = 1, "Improving" = 3)

# I experimented with weighting the SVM but quickly found that it was not
# enough. The model consistently predicted Stable due to the class imbalance.
# Various methods of correcting the class imbalance were investigated, however, 
# constrained as I was with working with a SVM, the results were not good. I
# tried using both SMOTE and ADASYN, but did not receive viable results for
# either. Hence, I realized that I needed to bring in G2 if I wanted the SVM to
# produce any valid results.

### Math SVM with G2 Data
set.seed(123)
# Creating data splits that include G2
df_math_change <- d1_math_clean %>%
   mutate(G2 = as.numeric(G2),
          G3_progress = G3 - G2) %>%
   mutate(progress_segment = cut(G3_progress, 
                                 breaks = c(-Inf, -0.1, 0.1, Inf), 
                                 labels = c("Declining", "Stable", "Improving"))) %>%
   select(-G1, -G3, -G3_progress)

# Ensuring that the data partition is not trying to partition an empty section
df_math_change$progress_segment <- as.factor(df_math_change$progress_segment)
df_math_change$progress_segment <- droplevels(df_math_change$progress_segment)
success <- FALSE
while (!success) {
  m_splitting <- try(createDataPartition(df_math_change$progress_segment, 
                                         p = 0.8, 
                                         list = FALSE), 
                     silent = TRUE)
    if (!inherits(m_splitting, "try-error")) {
    success <- TRUE
  }
}
m_train_data <- df_math_change[m_splitting, ]
m_test_data  <- df_math_change[-m_splitting, ]

m_train_data <- m_train_data %>% mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

library(caret)
# After a good deal of trial and error, I changed the method to svmLinear which
# gave me what I wanted, in that it is now attempting to predict on all three
# categories instead of only predicting Stable each time.
# I also changed the trControl to the following due to the svmLinear switch.
m_svm <- train(
   progress_segment ~ ., 
   data = m_train_data, 
   method = "svmLinear",
   trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10),
   preProcess = shared_preprocess,
   weights = shared_class_weights[m_train_data$progress_segment]
)

m_pred <- predict(m_svm, m_test_data)
m_table <- table(Predicted = m_pred, Actual = m_test_data$progress_segment)
print(m_table)
#                       Actual
# Predicted   Declining Stable Improving
# Declining         3      5         6
# Stable           13     29        15
# Improving         2      4         1
m_accuracy <- sum(diag(m_table)) / sum(m_table)
cat("Error Rate:", 1 - m_accuracy)
# Error Rate: 0.5769231

# Then I found the most important features.
m_importance <- varImp(m_svm, scale = TRUE)
plot(m_importance, top = 10, main = "Math: Top Factors Linked to Grade Decline")

# I knew I wanted to get the weighted values to see which ones had the greatest
# impact. I used Google AI for this to figure out how to get the weights out.
m_weights <- as.data.frame(t(m_svm$finalModel@coef[[1]] %*% m_svm$finalModel@xmatrix[[1]]))
m_weights$Feature <- rownames(m_weights)
colnames(m_weights)[1] <- "Weight"

m_top_social_issues <- m_weights %>%
   mutate(Importance = abs(Weight)) %>%
   arrange(desc(Importance)) %>%
   head(10)

ggplot(m_top_social_issues, aes(x = reorder(Feature, Importance), y = Importance)) +
   geom_point(size = 3, color = "darkred") +
   coord_flip() +
   theme_minimal() +
   labs(title = "Math: Social Issues Most Linked to Grade Decline",
        x = "Social/Academic Factor",
        y = "Relative Impact Strength")

# Ensuring that the data partition is not trying to partition an empty section

# The issue here for the Portuguese one is that this model is, again, not

### Portuguese SVM with G2 Data and New Index
library(themis)

# Ensuring that the data partition is not trying to partition an empty section
```

## Neural Network 

```{r nnetwork}
required_packages <- c("dplyr", "nnet", "caret", "ggplot2", "reshape2")
for (pkg in required_packages) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(pkg)
}

# 1. TARGET VARIABLE
# Binary classification: "Pass" (G3 >= 10) vs "Fail" (G3 < 10)
# Remove G3 = 0 rows (withdrawn / missing, per MasterData.R)
df_model <- df_clean %>%
  filter(G3 > 0) %>%
  mutate(Pass = factor(ifelse(G3 >= 10, "Pass", "Fail"),
                       levels = c("Fail", "Pass")))

cat(sprintf("Rows after filtering G3=0: %d\n", nrow(df_model)))
cat("Class distribution:\n")
print(table(df_model$Pass))

# 2. FEATURE SELECTION
# Drop raw grade columns to avoid data leakage:
#   - G1, G2 are intermediate grades; using them makes prediction trivial.
#   - G3 is what we derived Pass from.
#   - G3_progress (if present) would also leak.
drop_cols <- c("G1", "G2", "G3")
features  <- df_model %>% select(-all_of(drop_cols), -Pass)

# Dummy-encode all remaining factors
dummy_recipe <- dummyVars(~ ., data = features, fullRank = TRUE)
X <- predict(dummy_recipe, newdata = features)
X <- as.data.frame(X)

y <- df_model$Pass

cat(sprintf("Feature matrix: %d rows × %d columns\n", nrow(X), ncol(X)))

# 3. TRAIN / TEST SPLIT  (80 / 20, stratified)
set.seed(42)
train_idx   <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.80, list = FALSE)
X_train     <- X[train_idx, ]
X_test      <- X[-train_idx, ]
y_train     <- y[train_idx]
y_test      <- y[-train_idx]

# 4. CLASS WEIGHTS  (inverse-frequency weighting to penalise missed Fails)
# Weight for each training observation = N / (n_classes * class_count)
# This makes the network treat each Fail as ~3x more important than a Pass,
# proportional to the actual imbalance in the training set.
class_counts <- table(y_train)
n_total      <- length(y_train)
n_classes    <- length(class_counts)

class_weights <- n_total / (n_classes * class_counts)
cat(sprintf("\nClass weights  →  Fail: %.3f  |  Pass: %.3f\n",
            class_weights["Fail"], class_weights["Pass"]))

# Map each training observation to its weight
obs_weights <- ifelse(y_train == "Fail",
                      class_weights["Fail"],
                      class_weights["Pass"])

# 5. FEATURE SCALING  (min-max → [0, 1], fitted on train only)
preproc <- preProcess(X_train, method = c("range"))
X_train_sc <- predict(preproc, X_train)
X_test_sc  <- predict(preproc, X_test)

# 6. NEURAL NETWORK TRAINING  (nnet – single hidden layer, class-weighted)
cat("\nTraining neural network with 5-fold cross-validation (class-weighted)...\n")

# Custom summary so caret selects on F1 / Kappa rather than ROC
f1_kappa_summary <- function(data, lev = NULL, model = NULL) {
  # Standard two-class metrics
  two  <- twoClassSummary(data, lev = lev, model = model)
  # Default metrics (Accuracy, Kappa)
  def  <- defaultSummary(data, lev = lev, model = model)

  # F1 for the minority class (Fail = first level)
  cm_cv  <- confusionMatrix(data$pred, data$obs, positive = lev[1])
  f1_val <- cm_cv$byClass["F1"]
  if (is.na(f1_val)) f1_val <- 0

  c(two, def, F1 = as.numeric(f1_val))
}

ctrl <- trainControl(
  method          = "cv",
  number          = 5,
  classProbs      = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = f1_kappa_summary,
  savePredictions = "final"
)

# Wider decay range helps with class-weighted loss landscapes
grid <- expand.grid(
  size  = c(5, 10, 15, 20),
  decay = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5)
)

train_data <- cbind(X_train_sc, Pass = y_train)

set.seed(42)
nn_model <- train(
  Pass ~ .,
  data      = train_data,
  method    = "nnet",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid  = grid,
  metric    = "Kappa",        # optimise on Kappa; F1 also logged
  weights   = obs_weights,    # <-- inverse-frequency class weights
  maxit     = 500,
  trace     = FALSE,
  linout    = FALSE
)

cat("\nBest hyperparameters:\n")
print(nn_model$bestTune)

# 7. EVALUATION ON TEST SET
pred_prob  <- predict(nn_model, newdata = X_test_sc, type = "prob")

# --- 7a. ROC-AUC (threshold-independent) ------------------------------------
if (!requireNamespace("pROC", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pROC")
library(pROC)
roc_obj <- roc(y_test, pred_prob[, "Pass"], quiet = TRUE)

# --- 7b. Find the optimal threshold via CV probabilities --------------------
# Use the out-of-fold predictions saved during cross-validation to pick the
# threshold that maximises Kappa — this keeps threshold selection honest
# (no test-set peeking).
cv_probs  <- nn_model$pred                          # OOF predictions
cv_probs  <- cv_probs[cv_probs$size  == nn_model$bestTune$size &
                      cv_probs$decay == nn_model$bestTune$decay, ]

thresholds <- seq(0.30, 0.80, by = 0.02)

threshold_results <- sapply(thresholds, function(thr) {
  preds <- factor(ifelse(cv_probs$Pass >= thr, "Pass", "Fail"),
                  levels = c("Fail", "Pass"))
  cm_t  <- confusionMatrix(preds, cv_probs$obs, positive = "Pass")
  c(Kappa   = as.numeric(cm_t$overall["Kappa"]),
    F1      = as.numeric(cm_t$byClass["F1"]),
    BalAcc  = as.numeric(cm_t$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"]))
})

threshold_df         <- as.data.frame(t(threshold_results))
threshold_df$threshold <- thresholds

best_thr <- threshold_df$threshold[which.max(threshold_df$Kappa)]
cat(sprintf("\nOptimal CV threshold (max Kappa): %.2f\n", best_thr))

# --- 7c. Apply both thresholds and compare ----------------------------------
make_preds <- function(thr) {
  factor(ifelse(pred_prob[, "Pass"] >= thr, "Pass", "Fail"),
         levels = c("Fail", "Pass"))
}

pred_default <- make_preds(0.50)
pred_tuned   <- make_preds(best_thr)

cm_default <- confusionMatrix(pred_default, y_test, positive = "Pass")
cm_tuned   <- confusionMatrix(pred_tuned,   y_test, positive = "Pass")

print_metrics <- function(cm, label) {
  cat(sprintf("\n--- %s ---\n", label))
  cat(sprintf("  Accuracy        : %.4f\n", cm$overall["Accuracy"]))
  cat(sprintf("  Kappa           : %.4f\n", cm$overall["Kappa"]))
  cat(sprintf("  Sensitivity     : %.4f   (Fails correctly caught)\n",
              cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]))
  cat(sprintf("  Specificity     : %.4f   (Passes correctly identified)\n",
              cm$byClass["Specificity"]))
  cat(sprintf("  Precision       : %.4f\n", cm$byClass["Pos Pred Value"]))
  cat(sprintf("  F1 Score        : %.4f\n", cm$byClass["F1"]))
  cat(sprintf("  Balanced Acc.   : %.4f\n", cm$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"]))
  cat("  Confusion Matrix:\n")
  print(cm$table)
}

cat("\n")
cat("           NEURAL NETWORK – ACCURACY METRICS\n")
cat(sprintf("  ROC-AUC (threshold-independent) : %.4f\n", auc(roc_obj)))

print_metrics(cm_default, "Default threshold = 0.50")
print_metrics(cm_tuned,   sprintf("Tuned threshold  = %.2f  (CV-optimal)", best_thr))

# Keep cm pointing to the tuned model for the plots below
cm <- cm_tuned

# 8. PLOTS

# --- 8a. Confusion Matrix Heatmap ---
cm_df <- as.data.frame(cm$table)
colnames(cm_df) <- c("Predicted", "Actual", "Freq")

p_cm <- ggplot(cm_df, aes(x = Predicted, y = Actual, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 7, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#d6eaf8", high = "#1a5276") +
  labs(title = "Confusion Matrix – Neural Network",
       x = "Predicted Class", y = "Actual Class") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

print(p_cm)

# --- 8b. ROC Curve ---
if (exists("roc_obj")) {
  roc_df <- data.frame(
    FPR = 1 - roc_obj$specificities,
    TPR = roc_obj$sensitivities
  )
  p_roc <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(x = FPR, y = TPR)) +
    geom_line(colour = "#1a5276", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    annotate("text", x = 0.65, y = 0.15,
             label = sprintf("AUC = %.4f", auc(roc_obj)),
             size = 5, colour = "#1a5276") +
    labs(title = "ROC Curve – Neural Network",
         x = "False Positive Rate (1 – Specificity)",
         y = "True Positive Rate (Sensitivity)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
  print(p_roc)
}

# --- 8c. Cross-validation tuning profile (Kappa) ---
p_tune <- ggplot(nn_model$results,
                 aes(x = factor(size), y = Kappa,
                     colour = factor(decay), group = factor(decay))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(title  = "CV Tuning: Hidden Units vs Kappa",
       x      = "Hidden Units (size)",
       y      = "Cross-validated Kappa",
       colour = "Weight Decay") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

print(p_tune)

# --- 8d. Threshold sensitivity curve ---------------------------------------
thr_long <- reshape2::melt(threshold_df, id.vars = "threshold",
                           variable.name = "Metric", value.name = "Score")

p_thr <- ggplot(thr_long, aes(x = threshold, y = Score,
                               colour = Metric, group = Metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = best_thr, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = best_thr + 0.02, y = 0.15,
           label = sprintf("Optimal\n%.2f", best_thr),
           hjust = 0, size = 4, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Kappa  = "#1a5276",
                                 F1     = "#e67e22",
                                 BalAcc = "#27ae60")) +
  labs(title  = "Threshold Sensitivity (CV out-of-fold predictions)",
       x      = "Pass Probability Threshold",
       y      = "Score",
       colour = "Metric") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

print(p_thr)

cat("\nDone. Four plots have been rendered.\n")
```
